title: Quality Control
body:
Every order gets checked before it reaches the customer.

Designers: run `/qc` with your file and any notes. A reviewer approves it or sends it back with what to fix. Don't deliver anything that hasn't passed.

options.label: The Checklist
options.title: QC Checklist
options.content:
**Every submission**
Right dimensions and resolution. No stray layers, watermarks, or leftover placeholder text. Every name and title spelled correctly. The brief was actually followed.

**Liveries**
Sits correctly on the template, no bleed past safe zones, reads clearly at distance.

**Graphics**
Text is legible at small sizes. Exported clean with no compression artifacts.

**Bots and sites**
Runs without errors on a fresh setup. No hardcoded IDs left in.

options.label: Submitting Work
options.title: Submitting Work
options.content:
Run `/qc` with your image and a short note on what it is and anything you're unsure about.

It posts to the QC channel for a reviewer to pick up. You get a DM either way.

Submit before you show the customer, not after. Sending work back that a customer already saw is a worse look than a short delay.

options.label: Getting Sent Back
options.title: Changes Requested
options.content:
A reviewer sending work back isn't a punishment. Fix what they flagged and run `/qc` again.

If you disagree with the call, say so in the QC channel and let a higher rank settle it. Don't deliver over a reviewer's head.

Repeatedly skipping QC or ignoring feedback is an infraction, not a style difference.

options.label: For Reviewers
options.title: For Reviewers
options.content:
Be specific. "Fix the text" wastes a round trip. "The department name is misspelled on the rear quarter" doesn't.

Approve work that meets the standard even if you'd have done it differently. QC is for catching mistakes, not enforcing your taste.

Clear the queue quickly. Work sitting in QC is a customer waiting.
